artboards.title: The Sign in tab, signed in

annotations.text:
Start here — this artboard is live.

A vault with a passkey and a password enrolled, an authenticator code on top, and a Google account signed in through shoo.dev. Press the square to take step 1, then step 2. Toggle MFA off to see the rail disappear; toggle PIN on to see a third tab appear — tabs are exactly what the vault enrolled. Sign out to read what the device can and cannot end.

The account menu gains its exits.

The who@ segment already switched org profiles. It now names the identity at the top and carries the three roads the shell never had: attach another account, switch to a different one, or sign out — which ends the Identity session, forgets the shoo assertion and locks.

Enrolling MFA asks for a code first.

Today the gate is written the moment Enroll is pressed, before anyone proved the scan worked — and a guest could enroll it with no key at all, sealing a vault nothing can open. Now the row is withheld until a primary method exists, and the seed is written only once a code matches.

The whole flow on one page.

Two ledgers: who (the account) and key (the vault). Each has its own exit. The unlock screen states both, and neither is ever allowed to stand in for the other. The bottom row is what changes for enrollment, and what the screen says about a vault that already got it wrong.
